assessment.reason: Jax's start is confirmed by dated reporting. The 4.35 strikeout projection clears 3.5 by almost a full strikeout, and the model sits above the -125 break-even. The main risk is how long a converted reliever stays in a postseason game.
assessment.model_case: Recent workload averaged 13.29 outs per start, about 18 batters. At his strikeout rate against a modest-strikeout Cleveland lineup, that yields roughly four or more. The projection leans on that length; an early hook near 12 outs puts it close to the line.
assessment.price_case: BetMGM is offering 3.5 at -125. Paired consensus across five other books lands only slightly above the break-even, so the model, not the market, carries the gap. No alternate ladder is supplied.
assessment.context_case: Reporting establishes the planned start and a September ramp-up after an August injury. Postseason leash and bullpen plans are not reported.

qualitative_review.countercase: A ramped-up reliever in an ALCS game may face the order only twice. Contact-oriented hitters who know him from his Twins days could hold him to three strikeouts even with normal effectiveness.
open_checks: Reconfirm that 3.5 at -125 is still available near first pitch (1 p.m. ET).
Review published Cleveland batting order for left/right mix and strikeout profile.

evidence.interpretation: If this holds, the model's starter assumption matches the planned role. It does not confirm final active status or length.

assessment.reason: A projected home margin of only about a third of a run is hard to reconcile with a cover probability well above the +180 break-even. Consensus sits essentially at break-even, and the blended case shows almost no cushion.
assessment.model_case: The drivers are crude: recent runs per game and starter RA/9. A 0.33-run mean edge rarely supports winning by two or more, especially since Cleveland skips the bottom of the ninth when leading, which limits margin.
assessment.price_case: MyBookie.ag at +180 needs roughly a 36-in-100 chance to break even. Ten-book consensus is right at that level, so the price adds nothing over the market.
assessment.context_case: Only the rain-driven time change is reported. There is no lineup or bullpen reporting specific to the margin, and the offshore book's settlement rules for shortened games are unverified.

qualitative_review.countercase: Gavin Williams pitching at home against a recently injured converted reliever could produce a lopsided game. If the model's starter gap is real, the market may underrate Cleveland.

findings.note: CBS/RotoWire (Oct 14) confirms Jax starts ALCS Game 3, but says he hasn't gone five innings in a start in more than three weeks, so the Rays will need their bullpen for a big part of the game. That limits how many batters he faces.

VSiN says Jax has thrown only two innings since Sept 26 and questions how sharp he'll be on a damp day in Cleveland. It doesn't know how long he can go and expects Cleveland to swing early in counts. Its pick is Rays moneyline +110, not this prop.

MLB.com says Cash expects Jax to be full go after the line drive that hit his back ended his last regular-season start. Over his last five outings Jax struck out 19 in 20 innings, and Cash cited his starter work all season.
